IsWeak.maps_to: rooms.py::_hive_rooms().weak_keys (pool-membership relocation, not a property on Encounter)
IsWeak.rationale: ExoskeletonsWeak.cs:10 `IsWeak => true`. Same structural relocation as bowlbugs_weak's IsWeak: the sim's `Encounter` dataclass has no `is_weak` field; "exoskeletons_weak" is one of exactly two Hive keys in `_hive_rooms().weak_keys` (with "exoskeletons_normal" correctly absent from it, and present in `normal_keys` instead), which is what `RoomSet._generate_parity` reads to front-load the first `num_weak` rooms of the act. Behaviorally equivalent placement, structurally different representation.

Tags.rationale: ExoskeletonsWeak.cs:12 declares EncounterTag.Exoskeletons -- the SAME tag as the Normal variant (both share it, so the two never appear back-to-back per `GrabBag`'s tag-avoidance). `_hive_rooms()` pins the identical tag under "exoskeletons_weak", matching "exoskeletons_normal"'s tag too.

Slots.maps_to: exoskeleton.py::ExoskeletonsEncounter._SLOTS[:3] used as a per-monster constructor arg
Slots.rationale: ExoskeletonsWeak.cs:14 => ["first","second","third"] (3 slots, one fewer than Normal's 4 -- "fourth"/RAND-branch Exoskeletons never spawn in the Weak variant). Same load-bearing mechanism as exoskeletons_normal: `Exoskeleton.cs`'s `ConditionalBranchState("INIT_MOVE")` gates the opening move on `Creature.SlotName`; the sim's `Exoskeleton.__init__(slot=...)` + its own `ConditionalBranchState("INIT_MOVE")` (exoskeleton.py:61-68) reproduce the same three-way mapping. `EXOSKELETONS_WEAK = ExoskeletonsEncounter(id="exoskeletons_weak", count=3)` uses the same `_SLOTS` tuple, sliced by `range(self.count)` to just the first three ("first","second","third") -- the "fourth"/random branch is correctly never reached because `count=3` never iterates that far, matching the C# class's 3-element array never including it.

HasScene.maps_to: no counterpart -- sim is headless, no Godot scene graph
HasScene.rationale: ExoskeletonsWeak.cs:16 => true. Purely a rendering-asset gate, no headless equivalent, no gameplay consequence -- same rationale as every other HasScene=true unit in this batch.

RoomType.rationale: ExoskeletonsWeak.cs:18 => RoomType.Monster. "exoskeletons_weak" is placed in `_hive_rooms().weak_keys` (not `normal_keys`), matching the pool-classification convention used throughout this batch.

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: no per-encounter counterpart; full_env.py::_monster_classes() (global Monster-subclass walk)
AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: ExoskeletonsWeak.cs:20 declares a single-element list containing only `Exoskeleton` -- exactly GenerateMonsters' draw space (three copies). Same consumer census as the rest of the batch: only UI/debug readers exist for the C# property, and the sim's real vocabulary need is met by the global class walk. Cost: none observed.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: ExoskeletonsWeak.cs:22-30: three fixed `Exoskeleton` instances in slots "first","second","third" in that order, zero RNG draws. `ExoskeletonsEncounter.create_monsters` with `count=3` returns `[Exoskeleton(hooks, rng, slot=self._SLOTS[i]) for i in range(3)]` -- same 3 instances, same slot order, zero draws. Roster, order, slots and draw count all match.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: `EncounterModel.cs:39` default (`=> false`), not overridden by the sealed `ExoskeletonsWeak`. The sim's `Encounter` is never a hook listener.

guards.what: Gold ladder (MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward) and ShouldGiveRewards -- both inherited, not overridden by ExoskeletonsWeak
guards.rationale: RoomType.Monster => 10-20 gold, matched by `rewards.py:170-173`'s `GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]` (non-ascension baseline). `ShouldGiveRewards` default `true` matched by `Encounter.should_give_rewards`'s dataclass default, unmodified by `EXOSKELETONS_WEAK = ExoskeletonsEncounter(id="exoskeletons_weak", count=3)`.
